corrections.finding: Unclear: the closing apposition 'the great-great-grandchildren of the monarchs leaving those trees' reads as describing each monarch making the round trip, but the source says the arrivals are the great-great-grandchildren; also the east-to-Mexico, west-to-California split is lost, so 'or' reads as a free choice.
corrections.fixed_text: A year's monarchs are an overwintering generation and three or four summer generations; monarchs coming out in late summer and early fall are biologically and behaviorally different, not mating or laying eggs until the next spring, living some eight or nine months against three to five weeks for a summer adult, going up to three thousand miles south, eastern monarchs to oyamel fir forests in central Mexico and western monarchs to California's coastal groves, often to the exact same trees, and each making the round trip once, the monarchs arriving at those trees being the great-great-grandchildren of the monarchs leaving them the spring before. No monarch going south has a prior of its own there: a monarch's going is its kind's artifact of prior living with milkweed and with a winter forest, its stable form aiming an autumn monarch into healthy living, and a year's generations one same-existing-society going round one year.

corrections.finding: Stronger than source: 'of 26 eels ... six reach' drops that only 23 tags gave data (six of 26 vs six of 23), and 'satellite' is not in the source; also 'its larvae' has no clear antecedent (reads as the Sargasso Sea's).
corrections.fixed_text: European eels live as adults in Europe's fresh waters and go 5,000 to 10,000 km across the Atlantic to the Sargasso Sea to spawn, eating nothing on the way, diving to about 1,500 m by day and rising to about 200 m by night, some 3 to 12 km a day, a going of perhaps 18 months; of 26 eels with tags from the Azores, 23 tags giving data, six reach the Sargasso Sea, the first direct evidence of adults there, and the eels' larvae drift back to Europe on the North Atlantic Drift. An eel's going is its kind's artifact of prior living, its stable form aiming an eel to where its kind's living opens, a depth going with day and night and a larva's drift going with a current, each a co-sequencing.

corrections.finding: Saying places magnetism as what a turtle observes: 'whether a turtle learns its home's field' makes the field the turtle's learned object (the field is an instrument's record from outside); also 'with a like reading alike' is garbled and 'its authors' has no antecedent.
corrections.fixed_text: Loggerhead turtles nesting on beaches where an instrument reads a like magnetic field are genetically like each other, more than turtles on beaches near each other or of a like environment, turtles on Florida's two coasts where an instrument reads a like field being genetically like each other too; the study's authors ask whether a turtle learns its home or its genome gives it. A self observing reads a going-with: a turtle's coming home is its kind's artifact of prior living and its own prior same-existing now-existing in it, an instrument's reading at a beach going with that from outside a turtle's surface, and learning-or-genome a store question over one artifact of living.
